title: Supported by the Word
description: Supported by the Word in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 73, “The power and triumph of faith. Dan 3:6”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sup-port-ed by the word, Though in him-self a worm, The ser-vant of the Lord Can won-drous acts per-form: With-out dis-may he bold-ly treads Wher-e'er the path of du-ty leads.

lines: Where'er the path of duty leads.
The furnace could not make them fear,
Because they knew the Lord was near.
Which charged them not to pray;
Trusting in God, he feared not men,
Though threatened with the lion's den.
For what had they to lose,
He made the hungry lions crouch,
Nor durst the fire his children touch.
The Lord is still the same,
And they who trust his name
He can the rage of lions tame,
And bear them harmless through the flame.
But could we once believe indeed,
From all these fears we should be freed.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
